claims.text: A thin, adherent alumina coating will enhance the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components.
Alumina can serve as a high-temperature-stable barrier between molten aluminum and a boride substrate.
Boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment lack an intrinsic protective barrier.
Uncoated boride-based components corrode rapidly in high-temperature molten aluminum.
A thin alumina coating can be applied by sputter deposition.
Temperatures around 660–700 °C are characteristic of hot-dip aluminum-plating exposure.
The intervention will produce a continuous and adherent alumina layer.
The alumina layer will be a robust, chemically inert interfacial barrier under molten-aluminum exposure.
A continuous alumina coating will prevent direct contact between molten aluminum and the boride substrate.
The alumina barrier will inhibit interfacial chemical reactions and elemental dissolution.
Alumina can act as an effective diffusion barrier against further oxidation in suitable oxidative environments.
Coated components will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than uncoated components during molten-aluminum exposure.
The alumina coating will increase component longevity relative to uncoated boride-based components.
The coating should remain effective during prolonged molten-aluminum exposure at 660–700 °C under static or moderate mechanical stress.
Extreme thermal cycling, mechanical wear, or coating defects may compromise coating performance.
Optimal coating thickness, deposition parameters, and long-term adhesion under cyclic thermal stress remain undetermined.
The controlled test will compare sputtered-alumina-coated and uncoated boride specimens exposed to molten aluminum at 700 °C for 100 hours.
Corrosion will be evaluated using penetration depth, weight loss, and interfacial or surface microstructural analysis.
The hypothesis will be falsified if coating fails to produce a statistically significant corrosion-rate reduction of at least 15% relative to the uncoated control.
